newsitem.title: USA: Party control of six House seats undecided.
newsitem.headline: Party control of six House seats undecided.

text.p: One week after the election, the question of which party will control six House seats remained up in the air on Tuesday.
Republicans won 225 House seats, Democrats 203 and a single Independent was elected in the 435-member House of Representatives.
So far, Democrats hold five more seats than they did before the 104th Congress adjourned but the size of the loss for Republicans -- who had 235 seats -- was not yet clear.

In California, two veteran House members were waiting for mail and disputed ballots to be counted. California Republican Representative Bob Dornan was waiting for final results in his race against Democrat Loretta Sanchez, while California Democratic Representative George Brown was waiting for final results against Republican Linda Wilde.

In Washington state, mail ballots were still being tallied in close races for two Republican freshmen. Republican Linda Smith was waiting for the outcome against Democrat Brian Baird and Republican Jack Metcalf was waiting for results against Democrat Kevin Quigley.

The seats of two Texans will be decided in a special run-off election on Dec. 10. Republican Representative Steve Stockman faces Democrat Nick Lampson and Democratic Representative Ken Bentsen faces Republican Dolly Madison McKenna.
Because of late redistricting, run-offs were required in several Texas districts where no candidate won a majority.
Another Texas district will also be decided on Dec. 10, but party control was not at stake because the race is between two Republicans -- Kevin Brady and Gene Fontenot.

Additionally, several recounts were under way. They included the race between freshman Representative Jon Fox of Pennsylvania and Democrat Joseph Hoeffel. Fox won by only 10 votes out of nearly one-quarter of a million cast.
